svg.title: Imputation strategies for missing values
svg.desc: Reference card covering Mean/Median/Mode, Forward/Backward Fill, KNN, Regression, and Multiple Imputation strategies.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('When should I use mean vs median vs mode imputation?')
g.text: Simple and fast. Choose based on data type and distribution.
Mode risk: increases bias, ignores feature relationships, may distort class distribution

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does forward and backward fill work in time series?')
g.text: Best for time series data where row order matters.
Fills NaN with previous row's value
Fills NaN with next row's value
Finds K most similar rows and uses their values to estimate the missing value.
Works for both numerical and categorical columns. Smarter than mean/mode.
Builds a regression model using other columns to predict the missing value.
Uses relationships between features. More accurate than simple mean/median.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Explain multiple imputation step by step')
g.text: Most statistically robust. Creates N datasets, each with slightly different
imputed values (prediction + random noise), then averages all results.
Final result = average of all dataset analyses
When mode risks distorting data → use KNN or Multiple Imputation instead
